transcript.text: The sides of our new fridge freezer get really warm, almost hot, especially near the front edge. Is that a fire risk? It's in an alcove between two units.

Usually, no: warm—even very warm—outer sides and the front edges are commonly normal on a fridge-freezer. Those areas can carry tubing that dumps heat removed from inside, and it can feel hotter while a new appliance is settling down or working hard after loading. The alcove is the important part: if there is not the ventilation gap specified in its installation instructions, heat cannot escape efficiently and it will run hotter and use more electricity. Check the required side, rear and top clearances in the leaflet and make sure no vents are covered. Stop using it and arrange an inspection if there is a burning/hot-plastic smell, scorching, smoke, a damaged plug or socket, or it is tripping the electrics.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
Thanks, that's reassuring. There's no burning smell, no scorching and nothing tripping. The gap is only about 1cm each side, with a cupboard above and a few cm of space over the top. Is that enough?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Not necessarily. A 1 cm gap at each side and only a few centimetres above may be too tight for some fridge-freezers, particularly when boxed into an alcove; the required clearance varies by model, so the installation leaflet is the deciding guide. The warm front edges are still most likely normal heat-dumping tubing, but restricted airflow can make them noticeably hotter and make the appliance run longer. Check that it also has the required rear gap and that any ventilation grille or gap at the top/rear of the housing is not blocked. If the leaflet calls for more space, pull it forward or alter the housing clearance rather than continuing to run it tightly enclosed.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I'd rather not pull it out, we've just had new flooring laid and I'm worried about scratching it. The manual says to leave space but I haven't checked exactly how much. Is there another way to work out whether the gaps are enough?

Not reliably from how hot the sides feel: a fridge-freezer can cool normally yet still have insufficient ventilation, and 1 cm may be adequate for one design but too little for another. You should not need to pull it out to establish the requirement—look in the manual under “Installation”, “Ventilation” or “Clearances”; it is often a small diagram with minimum side, top and rear dimensions. The absence of smell, scorching or electrical tripping makes this sound much more like normal heat dissipation, possibly made warmer by the alcove, rather than an immediate fire-risk symptom. If the manual requires more clearance than is available, the safe answer is to have the housing altered or the appliance repositioned rather than relying on touch temperature.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
